name: Omar
title: Esau's grandson and Edomite tribal chief
summary: Omar was a son of Eliphaz and a grandson of Esau. He is mentioned in the Bible's genealogies as one of the tribal chiefs of Edom. Although he does not play a prominent role in biblical narratives, he is important as part of Edom's tribal history and Esau's lineage.

keyEvents.title: Omar's birth and lineage
keyEvents.description: Omar is mentioned as the second son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn. He is listed among Esau's descendants in the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Omar as a tribal chief in Edom
keyEvents.description: Omar is listed among the tribal chiefs (Hebrew: 'alluf') who descended from Eliphaz in the land of Edom. This shows his position as leader of an Edomite tribe.

keyEvents.title: Esau's genealogy repeated
keyEvents.description: Omar's lineage is repeated in 1 Chronicles as part of the great genealogy that begins with Adam, confirming his place in biblical history.

keyEvents.title: The patriarchs of Edom and the nation of Edom
keyEvents.description: Omar and his brothers formed the foundation of the Edomite tribes who settled in the mountains of Seir. Edom became a significant neighboring state to Israel throughout Old Testament history.
